tool.name: TIDDIT coverage
tool.description: compute binned read coverage from a BAM file
tool.command:
@LINK_BAM@
tiddit --cov --bam './${sample_name}.bam' -o coverage -z $bin_size -q $min_mapq
## TIDDIT reports its own errors on stdout and still exits 0. && if [ ! -s coverage.bed ]; then echo 'TIDDIT did not produce a coverage file; see the tool standard output for the reason.' >&2; exit 1; fi
## TIDDIT prints bin i as 1+i*z to (i+1)*z+1 (the last one ending at the ## contig length), which is neither BED nor 1-based closed. Rewrite it as ## 0-based half-open bedGraph without TIDDIT's header line. TIDDIT divides by ## the full bin size even when a contig is shorter than one bin, so rescale ## that case to the contig length. && awk -v bin=$bin_size 'BEGIN { OFS = "\t" } /^#/ { next } { s = \$2 - 1; e = s + bin; if (e > \$3) e = \$3; v = \$4; if (s == 0 && \$3 < bin) v = \$4 * bin / \$3; print \$1, s, e, v }' coverage.bed > coverage_fixed.bed
#if str($output_format) == 'wig': ## TIDDIT's own wig omits span, so each value would cover a single base. ## Build it from the BED instead, with a separate block for a short last bin. && awk 'BEGIN { print "track type=wiggle_0 name=\"Coverage\" description=\"Per bin average coverage\"" } /^#/ { next } { len = \$3 - \$2; if (\$1 != chrom || len != span) { print "fixedStep chrom=" \$1 " start=" (\$2 + 1) " step=" len " span=" len; chrom = \$1; span = len } print \$4 }' coverage_fixed.bed > coverage.wig #end if

param.name: min_mapq
param.label: Minimum mapping quality
param.help: Alignments with a lower mapping quality are not counted. Unmapped and duplicate-flagged reads are always skipped; secondary, supplementary and QC-failed alignments are counted.

tool.help:
## What it does
Computes the average read depth of a coordinate-sorted BAM file in fixed-size bins along every reference sequence, using the coverage module of [TIDDIT](https://github.com/SciLifeLab/TIDDIT). Unmapped reads, duplicate-flagged reads and reads below the mapping quality cutoff are not counted. Secondary, supplementary and QC-failed alignments are counted like any other alignment.
## Outputs
- **bedGraph**: one line per bin with chromosome, start, end and mean coverage, in 0-based, half-open coordinates (the first 500 bp bin is `0-500`). The last bin of each sequence ends at the sequence end and may be shorter than the bin size. - **Wiggle**: a `fixedStep` track whose `span` equals the bin size, with a separate block for a shorter last bin, suitable for genome browsers.
TIDDIT's own BED and Wiggle files are off by one base and lack `span` respectively, so this tool rewrites TIDDIT's bins into correct coordinates.
## Known limitation
TIDDIT 3.9.7 underestimates the coverage of a last bin that is shorter than the bin size. When a sequence is shorter than one bin the tool corrects the value; for longer sequences the short last bin cannot be corrected from TIDDIT's output and reads too low. Choose a bin size that divides the sequence lengths, or ignore the last bin of each sequence.
